thread:
Liam (ACME-POC): Hey all, quick POC blocker: our Datadog logs are arriving but they don't have trace_id to correlate with traces in Console.
Chen (platform): Are you sending x-redwood-trace-id or relying on x-request-id? We prefer x-redwood-trace-id for span linking.
Liam (ACME-POC): We were using x-request-id. Example: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-request-id: poc-abc' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat'
Chen (platform): x-request-id is passthrough only. Try: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-redwood-trace-id: rwd-0xdeadbeef' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat'
Liam (ACME-POC): Switched to x-redwood-trace-id, Console shows spans now. Datadog still not extracting trace_id, it's nested under message.payload.json.trace.
Maya (sales-eng): Customer also asked if we can include raw request body in exports for debugging. Security?
Priya (security): Hosted drains redact potential PII by default. To export raw request bodies we require a signed DPA and either Dedicated/Private deployment or a dedicated drain with explicit approval. Also note retention defaults and encryption-at-rest details on Q7/Q12 of the questionnaire.
Chen (platform): For Datadog field extraction, you have two options: 1) set the exporter transform to "flat" so trace_id is a top-level field; 2) teach Datadog to parse nested JSON. In Console: Project -> Routes -> <route> -> Exports -> Export transform = flat. Terraform example below:
```
resource "redwood_route" "embed_route" {
  name = "acme-embed"
  match = "/v1/embeddings"
  export {
    provider = "datadog"
    include_trace = true
    transform = "flat"
  }
}
```
Chen (platform): If you're using our log forwarding lambda, ensure it doesn't stringify the payload. We send structured JSON when transform=flat.
Liam (ACME-POC): Good tip. We're also hitting 429s when sending bulk embedding batches during the POC. Any temporary workaround?
Chen (platform): Reduce embed batch size to ~64-128 and use exponential backoff on 429. For the POC we can provision a temporary dedicated pool to reduce tenant throttling; that'll cut 429s. I can kick that off with eng-exports if you confirm traffic window.
Maya (sales-eng): Please open a ticket to request the temporary pool and a quick check on Datadog parsing. @ExportBot can you create one?
ExportBot: Ticket ENG-12055 created: "ACME POC - datadog trace extraction + temp dedicated pool" assigned to eng-exports, priority P2, ETA 48h.
Priya (security): If they want raw logs, Liam please send a signed DPA request and specify retention and KMS requirements to security@redwood.ai. We'll schedule the compliance review.
Liam (ACME-POC): Will do. One more: how do we force-sample traces so we see more during testing?
Chen (platform): You can force-sample per request with header: x-trace-sampled: 1. Or raise per-route sampling in Console: Observability -> Tracing -> Sampling override (set to 10-25% for POC).
Liam (ACME-POC): Perfect. I'll change transform to flat, re-ingest a few test logs, and send the DPA if needed. Thanks. :thumbsup:
Maya (sales-eng): I'll follow up on the ticket and coordinate the temporary pool.
Chen (platform): Ping me if Datadog still misses the field; I can provide a sample payload and a quick regex/datadog parser snippet.
Liam (ACME-POC): Copy that. Testing now.
